heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Fiji
heroData.subtitle: Global Employment Simplified in the Pacific
heroData.description: Hire talent in Fiji without a local entity. Our EOR solutions handle compliant contracts, FNPF contributions, and 2025 tax withholding requirements.

steps.title: Contract Drafting & ERA Review
steps.description: Creation of employment agreements that fully comply with the Employment Relations Act 2007. This includes defining standard working hours (typically 40-48 hours depending on the industry) and rest period mandates.

steps.title: FNPF Registration (Employer/Employee)
steps.description: Mandatory registration with the Fiji National Provident Fund. For 2025, we ensure contributions are set at the new baseline of 10% employer and 8% employee.

steps.title: TIN & FRCS Compliance Audit
steps.description: Validation of the employee's Tax Identification Number with the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service. This step ensures that PAYE withholding is accurate from the first pay cycle.

steps.title: Direct Deposit Banking Setup
steps.description: Integration with local Fiji banking institutions (BSP, ANZ, Westpac) to facilitate seamless salary transfers in FJD.

steps.title: OHS Induction & Compliance
steps.description: Mandatory Occupational Health and Safety briefing as per the 1996 Act. We provide documentation for both on-site and remote employees to verify safety standards.

steps.title: Equipment & Resource Logistics
steps.description: Coordinating the delivery of IT hardware and secure access credentials. We also manage the enrollment in optional private medical schemes common in the Suva tech hub.

values: Mandatory pension scheme; rates updated for 2025 budget cycles.

values: Insurance premium based on role risk profile (BPO vs. Construction).

items.title: Permanent Establishment Risk
items.text: Independent contractors working 100% for a foreign firm may be reclassified as employees by the FRCS, leading to heavy fines. EOR eliminates this risk.

items.title: The '120-Day' Payoff Myth
items.text: In Fiji, termination notice scales with service time. Always ensure specific notice clauses are in the contract to avoid expensive summary dismissal claims.

items.title: Public Holiday Premiums
items.text: Fiji has a high number of public holidays. Employees working these days must receive at least 200% of their base hourly rate.

items.title: Probationary Standards
items.text: A 3-6 month probation period is the market standard. Termination during this window requires a shorter 7-14 day notice period.

items.title: Late FNPF Penalties
items.text: Missing the end-of-month contribution deadline triggers a non-negotiable 2% monthly interest penalty.

items.title: Employment Relations Act 2007
items.description: The primary governing statute for all workforce interactions in the Republic of Fiji.

items.title: FNPF Act 2011
items.description: Defines the legal obligations for social security and retirement savings collection.

items.title: TIN Registration Certificate
items.description: All employees must possess a verified TIN to be legally processed on a Fiji payroll.

items.title: Occupational Health & Safety Act
items.description: Mandates employer responsibility for providing a safe working environment, including for remote staff.

items.title: Relationship-First Culture
items.text: The 'Bula Spirit' is real. Invest time in social check-ins. A disconnected remote worker is significantly more likely to leave.

items.title: Village Commitments
items.text: Traditional and community ceremonies are vital. Candidates appreciate flexible PTO policies that accommodate village responsibilities.

items.title: English Fluency
items.text: Leverage Fiji's native-level English fluency for global roles. It is the official language of education and commerce.

faqs.question: Can an EOR sponsor work permits in Fiji?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the process is rigorous. You must prove that no qualified local candidate was available. Approval can take 3-4 months.

faqs.question: What are the standard working hours?
faqs.answer: The standard is 40-44 hours per week. Anything beyond this must be compensated at 1.5x (overtime) or 2.0x (Sundays/Holidays).

faqs.question: Is severance pay mandatory?
faqs.answer: It is not strictly mandatory for all roles but is often explicitly negotiated in senior contracts or industry Collective Agreements.

faqs.question: Is 13th-month pay common?
faqs.answer: No, it is not legally required. Performance-based annual bonuses are much more common in the private sector.

steps.title: Variable Data Intake
steps.description: Gathering monthly attendance, overtime logs, and taxable fringe benefits (company cars/accommodation).

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Applying the 20% resident income tax (for income >$30k) and the 8% employee FNPF deduction using the latest 2025 formulas.

steps.title: Electronic Payment (E-Filing)
steps.description: Preparing the monthly Electronic Filing (EF) for the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service. Must be filed by the 14th of the following month.

steps.title: FNPF Contribution Submission
steps.description: Uploading the Contribution Schedule (CS) to the FNPF portal and settling the total 18% liability (10% employer + 8% employee).

steps.title: Payslip Generation & Distribution
steps.description: Issuing digital, compliant payslips showing detailed breakdowns of allowances, deductions, and YTD balances.

steps.title: NemKonto / Direct Disbursement
steps.description: Executing bank transfers to local FJD accounts. We ensure payments hit accounts by the 25th to avoid month-end delays.

rows.label: Resident Income Tax
values: On income above $30,000 FJD per year.

rows.label: FNPF (Employer Share)
values: Monthly; mandatory for all local staff.

items.title: TIN Validation Requirement
items.text: Processing payroll for an employee without a valid TIN can result in the employer being held liable for the employee's unpaid taxes plus 100% penalties.

items.title: Year-End Reporting (Form P4)
items.text: Annual summary certificates (P4) must be issued to all employees by the end of February each year to facilitate their tax returns.

items.title: Fringe Benefit Tax (FBT)
items.text: Employers pay 20% FBT on non-cash benefits. It is better to provide cash allowances if the goal is to optimize the employer's tax position.

items.title: Contractor Withholding
items.text: In certain sectors, you must withhold 15% provisional tax for payments to local service providers exceeding $1,000 FJD.

items.title: Pay frequency
items.description: Bi-monthly (twice a month) is common for wages, while monthly is the standard for salaried professional staff.

items.title: Local Bank Account
items.description: While payments can be initiated from offshore, having a local FJD account reduces settlement times and transaction fees.

items.title: Data Storage (7 Years)
items.description: Fiji Law (Tax Administration Act) requires all payroll records to be stored and accessible for 7 years.

items.title: FRCS Audit Scope
items.description: Tax authorities have the right to request comprehensive digital payroll logs for the last 5 years with minimal notice.

faqs.question: What is the tax-free threshold for 2025?
faqs.answer: For resident individuals, the first $30,000 FJD of annual income is tax-free.

faqs.question: Can we pay employees in USD?
faqs.answer: Contracts can be denominated in USD, but the actual payout must normally be in FJD for local employees per Central Bank regulations.

faqs.question: Are FNPF contributions required for expatriates?
faqs.answer: FNPF is optional for expatriates on work permits. However, if they opt-in, the same 18% total contribution rules apply.

faqs.question: When are payroll taxes due?
faqs.answer: PAYE tax and SRT must be paid to FRCS by the 14th of the month following the payment date.

steps.title: FNPF Employer Share (10%)
steps.description: Employer contribution to the Fiji National Provident Fund, calculated on gross wages.

steps.title: FNPF Employee Share (8%)
steps.description: Mandatory deduction from employee gross wages for retirement savings.

steps.title: PAYE Tax Deduction
steps.description: Pay-As-You-Earn tax withheld based on the annual resident tax bands.

steps.title: SRT (Social Responsibility Tax)
steps.description: Surcharge for high-income earners (>$270k) ranging from 5% to 25%.

steps.title: ECAL (Environment & Climate Adaptation)
steps.description: Now frequently consolidated with other taxes, but historically applicable to high-income thresholds.

items.title: Tax-Free Threshold
items.text: Fiji has a generous tax-free threshold of $30,000 FJD, which is high compared to regional neighbors.

items.title: FNPF Rate Stability
items.text: Current rates (10% employer / 8% employee) went into effect on January 1, 2024, and have been maintained for 2025.

items.title: Director Fees
items.text: Director fees are usually subject to WHT (Withholding Tax) rather than PAYE if the director is a non-resident.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, bonuses and commissions are treated as taxable income and should be included in PAYE calculations.

faqs.question: What is the payroll filing deadline?
faqs.answer: Employers must remit PAYE and FNPF schedules by the 30th of the following month.

faqs.question: Can we pay in USD?
faqs.answer: While contracts can reflect USD, local statutory deductions and payouts to local bank accounts must be converted to FJD.

steps.title: Annual Leave Calculation
steps.description: Ensuring all accrued but unused leave is calculated at the regular rate of pay as per ERA 2007.

steps.title: Taxation of Lump Sums
steps.description: Applying the correct PAYE treatment for severance and leave encashment to avoid over-withholding.

steps.title: Final FNPF Remittance
steps.description: Liaising with FNPF to ensure the final contribution matches the final pay run exactly.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Fiji
heroData.subtitle: Strategic Business Setup in the Pacific Hub
heroData.description: Establish your legal presence in Fiji. We manage everything from Registrar of Companies (ROC) filing to Foreign Investment Registration and banking setup.

steps.title: Digital Profile Setup
steps.description: Creating an e-profile on the DigitalFiji website to gain access to the online Registrar of Companies (ROC) portal.

steps.title: FIRC Approval (Foreigners)
steps.description: Securing a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate from Investment Fiji. This requires a business plan and proof of minimum investment capital.

steps.title: Constitution & Share Allocation
steps.description: Drafting the company constitution and allocating shares. Private Limited Companies (Ltd) in Fiji can have between 1 to 50 shareholders.

steps.title: Official Registrar Submission
steps.description: Submitting the application for the CVR (Central Business Register) number. Processing time is typically 48-72 hours via the digital portal.

steps.title: Tax & VAT Activation
steps.description: Registering the new entity with the FRCS for Income Tax, VAT (if turnover >$100k), and Employer (PAYE) obligations.

steps.title: Corporate Bank Account Opening
steps.description: Navigating the KYC process with a local bank. This is often the longest step and requires physical presence or notarized documents.

items.title: VAT De-registration Threshold
items.text: If your taxable turnover falls below $100,000 FJD, you can apply for VAT exemption, significantly reducing your administrative burden.

items.title: Reserve Bank Clearance
items.text: Repatriating capital or profits above specific thresholds requires RBF approval. Ensure your initial capital injection is clearly documented.

items.title: Expatriate Employment Slots
items.text: FIRC holders are typically granted a set number of 'automatic' work permit slots for senior expatriate management.

items.title: Zone-Based Incentives
items.text: Setting up in a 'Declared Development Region' can provide extended tax holidays of up to 13 years for specific sectors.

items.title: Companies Act 2015
items.description: The modern legal framework that simplifies company administration and increases transparency.

items.title: Public Officer Appointment
items.description: All companies must formally appoint a person to be responsible for tax filings and official correspondence.

items.title: Electronic Registers
items.description: Companies are now required to maintain an electronic register of shareholders and beneficial owners.

items.title: Annual Audit Requirement
items.description: While small private companies may apply for exemptions, most medium-to-large entities must file audited accounts.

faqs.question: Do I need a local shareholder?
faqs.answer: No. In most sectors, 100% foreign ownership is permissible under the Foreign Investment Act.

faqs.question: Can I use a virtual office address?
faqs.answer: No. The ROC and FRCS require a physical registered office address in Fiji where records can be inspected.

faqs.question: What is the corporate tax rate?
faqs.answer: The standard rate is 20%. Companies that list on the South Pacific Stock Exchange can benefit from a 10% rate.

faqs.question: How long does name reservation last?
faqs.answer: A reserved business name is held for 30 days, during which the full registration must be completed.

items.title: Digital Invoicing

faqs.question: What standards are used in Fiji?
faqs.answer: Fiji has fully adopted IFRS for large entities and IFRS for SMEs for smaller businesses.

faqs.question: What is the standard financial year?
faqs.answer: Most companies use January to December, but you can apply to the FRCS to use your global parent's fiscal year (e.g., July-June).

faqs.question: Are digital signatures accepted?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Electronic Transactions Act, digital signatures are legally recognized for most corporate and accounting documents.

items.title: Director Residency

faqs.question: Can we lose our business license?

items.title: Fiduciary Responsibility

items.title: Public Officer Appointment

items.title: Annual General Meetings

steps.title: Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
steps.description: Filing of the annual Form C. Due by March 31st for companies with a Dec 31st year-end. Standard rate is 20%.

steps.title: Value Added Tax (VAT)
steps.description: Monthly or quarterly filing depending on turnover. The 12.5% unified rate must be strictly applied to all taxable supplies.

steps.title: Withholding Tax (WHT)
steps.description: Managing payments to non-residents (management fees, royalties, interest). Rates typically vary from 10% to 15%.

steps.title: Capital Gains Tax (CGT)
steps.description: Reporting of gains on the disposal of Fiji assets. The standard CGT rate is 10%.

steps.title: Fringe Benefit Tax (FBT)
steps.description: Quarterly filing for benefits provided to employees. Effective rate is 20% on the grossed-up value of the benefit.

items.title: 2025 Tax Amnesty
items.text: The FRCS has announced a limited-time amnesty for the waiver of penalties on outstanding tax liabilities. Contact us for eligibility.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Inter-company transactions between Fiji subsidiaries and foreign parents must be at arm's length. Documentation is mandatory for values > $500k.

items.title: Advance Tax Rulings
items.text: For complex transactions, we can apply for a binding private ruling from the FRCS to gain certainty on tax treatment.

faqs.question: What is the VAT registration threshold?
faqs.answer: Compulsory registration is required if your annual taxable turnover exceeds $100,000 FJD.

faqs.question: Does Fiji have double tax treaties?
faqs.answer: Yes, Fiji has treaties with several countries including Australia, New Zealand, UK, India, and China to prevent double taxation.

faqs.question: Is there a dividend tax?
faqs.answer: Dividends paid by Fiji-resident companies are generally exempt from further tax in the hands of shareholders.

items.title: Mobile-First Design
items.text: Over 90% of web traffic in Fiji is mobile. Websites and landing pages must be extremely lightweight for local 4G speeds.

items.title: The 'Bula' Factor
items.text: Optimism and community focus are cultural cornerstones. Imagery showing local families and groups outperforms solo corporate stock photos.

faqs.question: What is the best platform for B2C sales?
faqs.answer: Facebook Marketplace and sponsored post groups are the most active e-commerce channels in the islands.

faqs.question: How do we target expatriates and tourists?
faqs.answer: Hyper-local geo-fencing around Nadi airport and major Denarau resorts via Google and Meta is highly effective.

faqs.question: Is TikTok popular in Fiji?
faqs.answer: Usage is surging among Gen-Z, making it the fastest-growing platform for creative lifestyle brands in 2025.

items.title: Social Commerce Surge
items.text: Fijian consumers increasingly purchase directly via Facebook Messenger and WhatsApp communities.

items.title: High Data Costs
items.text: Video ads should be high-impact but short to respect consumer data limits on mobile pre-paid plans.

items.title: Vernacular SEO
items.text: Optimizing for local search terms in iTaukei and Fiji Hindi is an untapped opportunity for organic growth.
